description: Golden set over the bundled Kestrel Labs corpus. A retrieved chunk is relevant to an expected item when it comes from that document and contains at least one evidence string (case- and whitespace-insensitive). Evidence strings, not chunk ids, keep the labels valid across chunking strategies.

questions.question: What is the API rate limit per workspace?
questions.reference: 600 requests per minute per workspace, with a burst allowance of 100.

questions.question: What HTTP status and error code does Relay return when a client is throttled?
questions.reference: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with error code KR-1029 and a Retry-After header.

questions.question: What does error KR-4291 mean?
questions.reference: An idempotency key was reused with a different payload (HTTP 409).

questions.question: How many delivery attempts does Relay make before giving up on an event?
questions.reference: At most 8 attempts; then the event moves to the dead-letter queue.

questions.question: What is the retry schedule for failed webhook deliveries?
questions.reference: Exponential backoff: 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 1 h, 6 h and 24 h after the previous attempt.

questions.question: How long are dead-lettered events kept?

evidence: Dead-lettered events are kept for 14 days

questions.reference: 14 days.

questions.question: How can a receiver verify that a webhook really came from Relay?
questions.reference: By checking the Kestrel-Signature header, an HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp and raw body using the signing secret.

questions.question: How old can a webhook timestamp be before the receiver should reject it?
questions.reference: More than 5 minutes away from the receiver's clock should be rejected.

questions.question: How long does the previous API key stay valid after a rotation?
questions.reference: 24 hours.

questions.question: What is the maximum page size for list endpoints?
questions.reference: 200 items (default 50).

questions.question: When does version 2 of the API reach end of life?
How many days of paid time off do employees get?
questions.reference: 25 days per calendar year plus local public holidays.

questions.question: How many unused vacation days can I carry over into next year?
questions.reference: Up to 5 days, which expire on 31 March.

questions.question: What are the core hours?
questions.reference: 13:00 to 16:00 UTC, Monday to Thursday.

questions.question: How long is parental leave?

evidence: 20 weeks of fully paid parental leave

questions.reference: 20 weeks, fully paid.

questions.question: How much is the home office stipend?
questions.reference: A one-time 1,200 USD stipend plus 50 USD per month for internet and co-working.

questions.question: What is the yearly budget for courses and conferences?
questions.reference: 1,500 USD per year; it does not roll over.

questions.question: How much are engineers paid for an on-call week?
questions.reference: A flat 350 USD per week, plus a day off in lieu if paged out of hours more than twice.

questions.question: How quickly must the primary on-call engineer acknowledge a page?
questions.reference: Within 10 minutes, otherwise it escalates to the secondary.

questions.question: How often are laptops replaced?
questions.reference: Every 3 years, or earlier if the hardware fails.

questions.question: What caused the delayed deliveries on 14 March 2025?
questions.reference: The TLS certificate presented by the Heron broker expired; it had been issued manually outside the automated renewal system.

questions.question: How long did the March 2025 delivery incident last?
questions.reference: 47 minutes, from 09:12 to 09:59 UTC.

questions.question: What share of EU deliveries was delayed during the incident?
questions.reference: Roughly 18% of deliveries in the EU region.

questions.question: Why did detection of the Heron incident take nine minutes?
questions.reference: The lag monitor evaluates once per minute and needed five consecutive breaches of its 5-minute threshold.

questions.question: Which action items came out of the certificate expiry postmortem?
questions.reference: Move Heron certificates to automated renewal, alert 21 days before expiry, tighten the lag alert, update the runbook and run a game day.

questions.question: How often are data encryption keys rotated?
questions.reference: Every 90 days.

questions.question: How long are event payloads retained on the Growth plan?
questions.reference: 30 days.

questions.question: What is the largest bug bounty reward?
questions.reference: Up to 5,000 USD for critical issues.

questions.question: Where should security researchers report vulnerabilities?
questions.reference: security@kestrel.example; reports are acknowledged within 2 business days.

questions.question: How much does the Scale plan cost?
questions.reference: 399 USD per month, including 10 million events.

questions.question: What is the overage price on the Growth plan?
questions.reference: 0.40 USD per 10,000 additional events.

questions.question: What discount do I get for paying annually?
questions.reference: 15% off the plan price (not on overage).

questions.question: How much service credit do Scale customers get when availability drops below the SLA?
questions.reference: 10% of the monthly fee per full 0.1% below 99.95%, capped at 50%.

questions.question: What happens when a free workspace runs out of events?
questions.reference: Publishing is paused until the next billing cycle; there is no overage on Starter.

questions.question: When do new engineers join the on-call rotation?

evidence: after completing their onboarding shadow shifts

questions.reference: After two shadow shifts in weeks five and six, typically in their seventh week.

questions.question: Which laptops can new engineers choose from?
questions.reference: A 14-inch MacBook Pro or a Framework Laptop 16 running Linux.

questions.question: What is the internal deploy tool called and how does it roll out changes?
questions.reference: Kite; staged rollout to 1%, then 10%, then everyone, with automatic rollback if the error rate doubles.

questions.question: By when must the security training be completed?
questions.reference: By the end of week three.

questions.question: Did the March 2025 incident break the Scale plan SLA, and what credit does that give?
questions.reference: Yes: EU availability fell to 99.89%, below 99.95%; the credit is 10% of the monthly fee per full 0.1% below target.
